DESAI ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENT NO.1: SRI.GURURAJ KULKARNI ADVOCATE FOR RESPODNENT NO.2-SRI.A.N.SOMEGOWDA ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENT NO.3-SRI.S.MAHESWARA JUDGMENT This is a petition filed by the petitioners u/s 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.5,00,00,000/ with interest from respondents on account of death of Goutham Krish S. in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief:
That on 2372017 at about 7.10 a.m. when deceased was riding his bike bearing reg.no.TN22CX4783 in front of Gujarat Petrosynthese Limited, Doddanekkundi,
Bengaluru and back side road of Graphite India factory, driver of the mini tempo bearing No.KA01AB3641 came in a rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased bike bearing No.TN 22CX4783 which resulted in severe injury to Goutham JUDGMENT Krish S. and Goutham Krish was taken to Manipal hospital,
Bengaluru and was treated in ICU and succumbed to the injuries at hospital.
The petitioners have stated that deceased was flourishing operational professional career and earning Rs.42,238/p.m.

It is further stated that petitioners spent Rs.25,000/
towards funeral expenses and spent medical expenses of the deceased.
Goutham Krish was very intelligent and hard working and had great prospects in his professional and academic careers.
Due to death of Goutham Krish, petitioners lost their love and affection and put to shock and grief.
Hence petitioners prays to award compensation of Rs.5 crores from the respondents.
3. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 to 3 appeared before the court and only respondent No.3 filed written statement.

4. The respondent No.3 in its written statement contended that insured is duty bound to submit all vehicular documents, including driving licence before this respondent as mandated u/s 134 (c) of MV Act and there is a clear violation of provisions of law and contract of insurance.

As JUDGMENT per Sec.158(6) of MV Act, it is mandatory duty of the concerned police station to forward all the relevant documents to the concerned insurer within 30 days from the date of information, but the KR puram traffic police failed to forward the documents and not complied with the statutory demand.
It is further contended that the tempo bearing No.KA01AB3641 was not at all involved in the alleged accident.

The accident took place on 2372017, complaint was lodged on 2572017 Subramanian.K vs Bheemappa Ramachanddrappa Nayak on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181233958/
2 after lapse of 2 days from the date of alleged accidence.
This respondent specifically submits that tempo bearing No.KA01AB3641 was falsely implicated by the petitioners colluding with the insured and the police, to get the compensation by this respondent.
The tempo was not having valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

5. From the above said pleadings four issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioner prove that they are the legal representative of the deceased?

2. Whether the petitioners prove that Goutham Krish S S/o Subramanian K died due to injuries sustained JUDGMENT by him in an accident occurred on 2372017 at about 7.10 a.m., in front of Gujarath petro sentises, behind graphite India road,
Doddanekkundi, Bengaluru city, Karnataka560048, arising due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Tipper lorry bearing reg.No.KA01AB3641?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom?
4. What Order or Award?

My answers to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 & 2 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative,
JUDGMENT Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following: REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.2 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Mini tempo bearing reg.No.KA01 AB3641, the petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 38 documents as ExP1 to 38 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report, panchanama, PM report, statement, cc No.317/2017 ordersheet copy, DL, voter ID, adhar card, marks card, degree certificates, form No.16, 12BA, pay slip, medical bills.
12.

Though the counsel for the respondent No.3 has made the suggestion that the accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased, but the same has outrightly denied by the PW1.

Though respondent No.3 taken the contention that the accident had been taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased, but has not examined the driver of the tempo respondent No.1 to JUDGMENT prove the same.

13. Apart from this, on the complaint lodged by one Aravindkumar, K.R.Puram traffic police registered the FIR and conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed charge sheet against the respondent NO.1.
The petitioner has produced ExP19 ordersheet in Crime No.317/2017 which was registered as CC No.35828/17 before MMTC I.

On perusal of which, it clearly shows that K.R.Puram police has filed the charge sheet against the respondent No.1 for the offence punishable u/s 279, 304A, 134(A & B), 187, 3(1), 181, 5, 180 of IMV Act and accused No.2 owner had plead the guilty in respect of the offence punishable u/s 134(A) r/w 187, 3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act and has paid the fine amount.
Moreover all these documents has not been disputed by the respondent counsel.
Even the respondent No.1 and 2 though appeared through their counsel but not filed written statement and contested the case.

14. Apart from this, on perusal of ExP3 spot panchanama and ExP4sketch, it clearly shows that the JUDGMENT accident had been taken place as respondent No.1 driver of the offending vehicle has driven the vehicle to the wrong side of the road.
The accident has been taken place on the right side of the road from whitefield towards Chinnappanahalli.

Thus ExP3 and ExP4 clearly shows Subramanian.K vs Bheemappa Ramachanddrappa Nayak on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181233958/
4
that the accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
15. Though respondent No.3 contented that there was a delay of two days in filing of complaint.
As per ExR4 MLC, it is stated in ExR4 with regard to the history of injury as RTA bike accident, near Graphite area, IFB company and as such the tempo is not involved in the accident.
Further it was argued by the counsel for the respondent No.3 that there was no damages to the tempo and as such the tempo was not involved in the accident.

In the line of argument adduced by respondent No.3 if materials on record are perused, respondent No.2 owner of the offending vehicle has not at all disputed the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
Moreover as per the spot mahazar ExP3 and ExP5 IMV report there was scratches on the right side body of the JUDGMENT tempo and even the tempo was seized as per ExP3.
Moreover respondent No.2 has pleaded guilty and also paid the fine as per the ordersheet ExP19.
All these documents is not disputed by the respondent No.3.
All these police documents coupled the evidence of the PW2 and also evidence of the PW1 clearly establishes that factum of accident and the involvement of the tempo in the accident.
16. Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of the mini tempo bearing No.KA01AB3641 and Goutham Krish S. died in the said accident.
As such, I answer issue No.2 in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUES NO.1 & 3 :
The petitioners have produced ExP20DL, ExP21voter ID, ExP22 Adhaar card, ExP23 and 24marks card, ExP25degree certificate.
From the said documents, it reveals that petitioner No.1 is the father, petitioner No.2 is the mother and petitioner No.3 is the JUDGMENT brother of the deceased Goutham Krish S..

18. This relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents,
as is evident from the tenor of cross examination of PW.1.

Be that as it may, since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
19. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS: In the PM report (Ex.P.7) the age of the deceased is shown as 26 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '17'.
20.
According to the petitioners, deceased was working as Senior operation professional at IBM India Pvt., Ltd., and earning Rs.42,238/p.m.
In support of their contentions, petitioners have produced ExP27form No.16, ExP28 to 32 form No.16,12 BA, ExP33 to 37 pay slips.
JUDGMENT 21.

From the above said documents, it clearly establishes that deceased was working as Senior operation professional at IBM India Pvt., Ltd., Though respondent counsel contended that petitioner has not adduced the evidence of the employer and produced the bank statement of the deceased to prove that deceased was working IBM India Pvt., Ltd., and drawing the salary, but on Subramanian.K vs Bheemappa Ramachanddrappa Nayak on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181233958/
5

perusal of the cross examination of the PW1, no where counsel for the respondent No.3 has denied the fact that deceased was working in the IBM company and drawing salary and even not lead any evidence to disprove that deceased was not working in IBM at the time of accident.

In the absence of evidence, this court can certainly rely on the documents produced by the petitioners and consider the same and come to the conclusion that at the time of accident deceased was working in the IBM company and drawing the salary.

22. On perusal of ExP27 to 32 Form No.16 for the year 20172018, 20182019 and form No.16,
12 A B, it reveals that deceased was working in the IBM company and also he JUDGMENT was an income tax assessee and was paying the income tax.

Since the accident has been taken place on 23 72017 and Goutham Krish succumbed to the injuries on 2572017 only the income from March 2017 to June 2017 only has been taken into consideration while assessing the income tax returns for the year 20172018 as per ExP27.
Hence, ExP27 to 32 cannot be relied on as it does not reveals the entire annual income of deceased.
23. However petitioner has produced salary slip ExP33 to 37 for March, April, May, June and August 2017.
As per ExP33 salary slip for the month of June 2017 deceased was drawing the salary of Rs.45,636/ and paying the professional tax of Rs.200/ and income tax of Rs.580/.
It is settled law that while ascertaining the actual income the amount paid towards professional tax and amount paid towards income tax has to be deducted.
As such after deducting the professional tax and income tax paid by the deceased the actual income of the deceased as on the date of JUDGMENT accident worksout to Rs.44,856/.

As such this tribunal has consider the income of deceased at Rs.44,856/p.m.
24.
As per Sarala Verma's case towards his future prospectus if 50% of the salary is added it would be around Rs.67284/ (Rs.44,856 + 22428).

As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SCC 5157, The deceased was bachelor and as such in view of the proposition of Law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma's case, half of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/2 of Rs.67284/ works out to Rs.33,642/.
Income for consideration is Rs.33,642/ (67284 - 33642).
Annual income works out to Rs.4,03,704/ (33642 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '17'.

Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.68,62,968/ (4,03,704 X 17)
which is rounded off to Rs.68,63,000/.
25.

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s.

MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The petitioners have stated that after the accident, the deceased was taken to Manipal hospital, KR Puram hobli, Bengaluru and the hospital authorities treated the deceased who was critically injured at that time in ICU.
The petitioners have produced ExP38 JUDGMENT medical bills for Rs.26,399/.

1 Loss of 68,63,00000 Dependency 2 Loss of 1,45,20000 Consortium 3 Loss of Estate 18,15000 4 Funeral 18,15000 Expenses 5 Medical 24,00000 expenses Total 70,68,500=00

Hence, petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.70,68,500=00.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate JUDGMENT of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
31. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of the policy and the validity of the policy as on the date of the accident.

The counsel for the respondent No.3 argued that the driver of the tempo Tipper lorry bearing No.KA01AB 3641 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the particular class of the vehicle as on the date of accident and respondent No.2 knowing fully well that the driver did not possess valid and effective DL as willfully entrusted vehicle to the said driver and thereby respondent No.2 has committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Hence, respondent No.3 is not liable to pay the compensation.

Further argued that even the jurisdictional police after through investigation has filed the charge sheet against respondent No.1 and 2 u/s 3(1) r/w 181 and Section 5 r/w 180 of IMV Act.
32.

In this regard on perusal of the ExP19 ordersheet produced by the petitioners themselves clearly shows that jurisdictional police after through investigation has filed JUDGMENT charge sheet against the respondent No.2 for offence punishable u/s 3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act.
even respondent No.1 and 2 have not disputed this fact and filed any written statement and disproved the ExP19.

thus it is clear that as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 was driving vehicle without holding valid and effective DL and the respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the said vehicle has allowed respondent No.1 who was not having valid licence to ride the vehicle and thereby committed the breach of the conditions of the policy.

34. In this regard this court has relied on decision reported in (2018) 3 Supreme Court cases 208 between Pappu Vs Vinod Kumar wherein the Hon'ble Apex court in para No.17 to 20 held that This issue has been answered in National insurance co., Ltd.,

In that case, it was contended by the insurance company that once the defence taken by the insurer is accepted by the Tribunal, it is bound to discharge the insurer and fix the liability only on the owner and /or the driver of the vehicle.

Subramanian.K vs Bheemappa Ramachanddrappa Nayak on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181233958/
7 JUDGMENT

However, this court held that even if the insurer succeeds in establishing its defence,
the Tribunal or the court can direct the insurance company to pay the award amount to the claimant(s) and in turn, recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
The three Judge Bench after analyzing the earlier decisions on the point, held that there was no reason to deviate from the said well settled principle.

35. In the case of third party risks, as per the decision in National Insurance Company Ltd. v.
Swaran Singh the insurer had to indemnify the compensation amount payable to the third party and the insurance company may recover the same from the insured.

sentences.text: Doctrine of "pay and recover" was considered by the Supreme Court in Swaran Singh case wherein the Supreme Court examined the liability of the insurance company in cases of breach of policy condition due to disqualifications of the driver or invalid driving licence of the driver and held that in case of third party risks, the insurer has to indemnify the compensation amount to the third party and the insurance JUDGMENT company may recover the same from the insured.

Elaborately considering the insurer's contractual liability as well as statutory liability visavis the claims of third parties, the Supreme Court issued detailed guidelines as to how and in what circumstances, "pay and recover" can be ordered.
In para (110), the Supreme Court summarised its conclusions as under: "110.

The summary of our findings to the various issues as raised in these petitions is as follows:
(i) Chapter XI of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 providing compulsory insurance of vehicles against thirdparty risks is a social welfare legislation to extend relief by compensation to victims of accidents caused by use of motor vehicles.
The provisions of compulsory insurance coverage of all vehicles are with this paramount object and the provisions of the Act have to be so interpreted as to effectuate the said object.

(ii) An insurer is entitled to raise a defence in a claim petition filed under Section 163A or Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, inter alia, in terms of Section 149(2)(a)(ii) of the said Act.

(iii) The breach of policy condition e.g. disqualification of the driver or invalid driving licence of the driver, as contained in subsection (2)(a)(ii) of Section 149, has to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.

Mere absence, fake or JUDGMENT invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.

To avoid its liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.

(iv) Insurance companies, however, with a view to avoid their liability must not only establish the available defence(s) raised in the said proceedings but must also Subramanian.K vs Bheemappa Ramachanddrappa Nayak on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181233958/
8 establish "breach" on the part of the owner of the vehicle; the burden of proof wherefore would be on them,
(v) The court cannot lay down any criteria as to how the said burden would be discharged, inasmuch as the same would depend upon the facts and circumstances of each case.

(vi) Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving licence is/are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.

The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose" and the concept of "fundamental breach"
to allow defences available to the insurer under Section JUDGMENT 149(2) of the Act.

(vii) The question, as to whether the owner has taken reasonable care to find out as to whether the driving licence produced by the driver (a fake one or otherwise), does not fulfill the requirements of law or not will have to be determined in each case.
(viii) If a vehicle at the time of accident was driven by a person having a learner's licence, the insurance companies would be liable to satisfy the decree.

36. In ILR 2020 KAR 2239 New India Assurance Company Ltd Bijapuar by its Divisional Manager /
Yallavva and another where in also similar observation is made and held that " the insurer is liable to pay the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any condition recognized under section 149(2), even if it is a fundamental breach and the insure proves the said breach I view of the mandate under section 149(1) of the Act.

sentences.text: But no such order can be passed against the insurer, if on the facts and circumstances of the case, a findings is given by the court that the third party ( injured or deceased ) had played any fraud or was in collusion with the insured JUDGMENT individually or collectively for a wrongful gain to themselves or cause wrongful loss to the insurer.
37. Applying the ratio laid down in the aforesaid ruling to the facts of the present case, admittedly deceased is a third party to the contract between respondent No.1 and 2.

In further it is not the case of the respondent No.3 and it is not even proved that there is a fraud played by the petitioners in collusion with respondent No.1 driver of the offending vehicle in order to get wrongful gain to themselves and wrongful loss to the insurer.

Under the given circumstances this court finds it just to order the respondent No.3 to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and then to recover the said amount from the respondent No.2 under pay and recovery theory.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent No.3, this court directs the respondent No.3 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of deposit of entire amount within one month and then to recover the said amount from the JUDGMENT respondent No.3.

Accordingly issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is Subramanian.K vs Bheemappa Ramachanddrappa Nayak on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181233958/
9 answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
38. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the findings given on issues No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
: ORDER :

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms: The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.70,68,500/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

The respondent No.3 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioners within 30 days from the date of this order, with liberty to recover the same from the insured/respondent No.2 in appropriate execution proceedings as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Since the accident has been taken place on 23 72017 and Goutham Krish succumbed to the injuries on 2572017 only the income from March 2017 to June 2017 only has been taken into consideration while assessing the income tax returns for the year 20172018 as per ExP27.
Hence, ExP27 to 32 cannot be relied on as it does not reveals the entire annual income of deceased.
As per ExP33 salary slip for the month of June 2017 deceased was drawing the salary of Rs.45,636/ and paying the professional tax of Rs.200/ and income tax of Rs.580/.
It is settled law that while ascertaining the actual income the amount paid towards professional tax and amount paid towards income tax has to be deducted.
As such after deducting the professional tax and income tax paid by the deceased the actual income of the deceased as on the date of JUDGMENT accident worksout to Rs.44,856/.
The counsel for the respondent No.3 argued that the driver of the tempo Tipper lorry bearing No.KA01AB 3641 was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the particular class of the vehicle as on the date of accident and respondent No.2 knowing fully well that the driver did not possess valid and effective DL as willfully entrusted vehicle to the said driver and thereby respondent No.2 has committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
In this regard on perusal of the ExP19 ordersheet produced by the petitioners themselves clearly shows that jurisdictional police after through investigation has filed JUDGMENT charge sheet against the respondent No.2 for offence punishable u/s 3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act.
even respondent No.1 and 2 have not disputed this fact and filed any written statement and disproved the ExP19.
thus it is clear that as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 was driving vehicle without holding valid and effective DL and the respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the said vehicle has allowed respondent No.1 who was not having valid licence to ride the vehicle and thereby committed the breach of the conditions of the policy.

(iii) The breach of policy condition e.g. disqualification of the driver or invalid driving licence of the driver, as contained in subsection (2)(a)(ii) of Section 149, has to be proved to have been committed by the insured for avoiding liability by the insurer.
Mere absence, fake or JUDGMENT invalid driving licence or disqualification of the driver for driving at the relevant time, are not in themselves defences available to the insurer against either the insured or the third parties.
To avoid its liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time.
(vi) Even where the insurer is able to prove breach on the part of the insured concerning the policy condition regarding holding of a valid licence by the driver or his qualification to drive during the relevant period, the insurer would not be allowed to avoid its liability towards the insured unless the said breach or breaches on the condition of driving licence is/are so fundamental as are found to have contributed to the cause of the accident.
The Tribunals in interpreting the policy conditions would apply "the rule of main purpose" and the concept of "fundamental breach"
to allow defences available to the insurer under Section JUDGMENT 149(2) of the Act.
(vii) The question, as to whether the owner has taken reasonable care to find out as to whether the driving licence produced by the driver (a fake one or otherwise), does not fulfill the requirements of law or not will have to be determined in each case.

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.
Hence by fastening liability on the respondent No.3, this court directs the respondent No.3 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of deposit of entire amount within one month and then to recover the said amount from the JUDGMENT respondent No.3.
In view of the findings given on issues No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
: ORDER :
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms: The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.70,68,500/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.3 is hereby directed to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest to the petitioners within 30 days from the date of this order, with liberty to recover the same from the insured/respondent No.2 in appropriate execution proceedings as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Oriental Insurance Company Ltd V/s Nanjappan & others reported in (2004) 13 SCC 224.
On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation JUDGMENT amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 30%
 Petitioner No.2 50%
 Petitioner No.3 20%
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 to 3 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in their respective name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to them through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioners are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw an award accordingly.
